question: Why is a client-state modal driven only by `?assetId=123` rejected when the product requires both an in-context gallery overlay and a standalone shareable asset page?
options: Next.js blocks query parameters inside Server Components

A query-parameter modal always requires loading the entire gallery route even on direct visits, whereas pairing `@modal/(.)asset/[id]` with `/asset/[id]` renders a lightweight overlay on soft navigation and a dedicated standalone Server Component page on hard navigation
Query parameters cannot be read on the client
explanation: With Parallel + Intercepting Routes, clicking from `/gallery` intercepts `/asset/42` into `@modal` over the gallery, while opening `/asset/42` directly in a new tab renders only the standalone asset route.

question: What is the primary operational risk of introducing multiple Parallel Route slots (`@invoices`, `@usage`, `@modal`) into a layout?
options: Parallel slots disable TypeScript type checking
Every slot must maintain a `default.tsx` fallback for unmatched sub-routes, otherwise hard browser reloads on a sub-route will fail with a 404
Parallel slots force all child components to become Client Components
explanation: On a hard reload, Next.js has no in-memory router state for unmatched slots and falls back to `default.tsx`; if any slot lacks both a matching segment and `default.tsx`, the whole route 404s.

question: Which routing convention lets `/pricing` and `/dashboard` use completely separate layouts without changing their URLs to `/marketing/pricing` and `/console/dashboard`?
explanation: Route Groups `(folder)` partition the layout tree while omitting the group name from the public URL path.

question: How do `error.tsx` boundaries inside Parallel Route slots (`@invoices/error.tsx` and `@usage/error.tsx`) improve dashboard resilience?
options: They automatically retry database queries on the server without re-rendering
They isolate runtime errors to the failing slot so sibling panels remain interactive and mounted while the failing slot shows its recovery UI
They convert all Server Components into static HTML at build time
They suppress all HTTP 500 status codes globally
explanation: Giving each parallel slot its own `error.tsx` boundary contains failures to that specific panel and lets users invoke `reset()` on the failed slot without losing state in healthy sibling slots.
